title: Estimating pig liveweight with a weigh tape
subtitle: You cannot weigh a pig with bathroom scales. A tape measure and one formula get you within 10%.
excerpt: A purpose-made pig weigh tape reads liveweight directly from heart girth and body length measurements, pre-converting the calculations. If you do not have a tape, the heart-girth formula takes thirty seconds with a dressmaker's tape and gives the same result. Here is how to take the measurements and use them.
sourceNotes: AHDB Pork smallholding management notes, weight estimation section. DEFRA animal welfare monitoring guidance. Carla Emery, Encyclopedia of Country Living (1994), chapter on estimating livestock weight.

glossaryTerms.definition: The circumference of a pig measured immediately behind the front legs. The primary measurement used in weight estimation formulas. Taken with a flexible tape.
The total weight of the living animal. For smallholding purposes: used to calculate feed rations and to assess progress toward slaughter weight.

aliases: how to weigh a pig without scales

content.text: Two people make this easier, one holds the pig's attention with food, one takes the measurements. A pig that is eating will stand still for the seconds the tape needs. The
measurement is the critical one; body length adds precision.
Stand the pig on flat ground with all four feet square. A pig leaning or with its weight on one side gives a slightly off reading.
Heart girth: pass the tape around the pig's body directly behind the front legs. Hold it snug but not compressed, you should not be squeezing the tape in. Read the measurement in cm.
Body length: run the tape from the base of the ear (not the tip) to the base of the tail. Read in cm.
Using a purpose-made pig weigh tape: line up the body length column with the heart girth row and read the
from the intersection. No arithmetic needed.
Using a standard tape and the formula:
Weight (kg) = (heart girth in cm × heart girth in cm × body length in cm) ÷ 14,400

Heart girth = 90 cm, body length = 80 cm. 90 × 90 = 8,100. 8,100 × 80 = 648,000. 648,000 ÷ 14,400 = 45 kg liveweight. A finishing pig at this weight is on a grower ration and a few weeks from the switch to a finishing ration.

Record the weight in the holding register alongside the date. Weigh every 2-3 weeks during the growing phase. A pig that should be gaining 0.5-0.7 kg per day and is not meeting that rate needs its ration reviewed or a health check.

Target slaughter weights vary by the end product. Pork (fresh cuts) at 60-75 kg liveweight. Bacon pigs at 80-100 kg. Heavy hogs for charcuterie at 110-130 kg. Book the abattoir slot 6-8 weeks ahead of the estimated target date based on current weight and daily gain.
